name: print that the sheet may be wrong and noticing counts
one_line: One printed sentence saying the task may have no answer and that showing so is a win, on forms that otherwise fail without saying anything.
how: Use it on anything that can be wrong in silence: cut-out pieces that will not close, a maze with no way through, a grid with two answers, a mate in two that is not one. The sentence is short — if the last line stays empty the task is not hard, it is broken, and finding that out is worth more than solving it. Give the test with it, because a licence without a test is only comfort: list every legal reply and answer each; walk the maze marking each entrance and stop when everything is marked twice; count the pieces. Then print a place to write which of the two it was. Whoever cannot finish then has two possibilities instead of one, and one of them is not about them.

knobs.knob: whether a test comes with the sentence
knobs.effect: With one — every legal reply listed, every passage marked twice — the claim that the sheet is wrong can be made and defended. Without one it is permission to stop, which is a different and worse thing to hand over.
On a form somebody verified, it costs a line and reassures. On every sheet it says the household prints things it has not checked, which may be true and is still not worth saying twice a week.

knobs.knob: whether the fault is given a name
knobs.effect: Chess composition calls a problem with two keys cooked and throws it out, and a choice of second moves a dual and tolerates it. Two words separate a fatal fault from a bearable one; «it does not work» covers both.

Nobody, when the test is exhaustive and printed: a full list of the opponent's replies is a proof and needs no reader. Somebody, when the claim is that a maze has no exit and the marking was never done.

where_the_work_is: In the test that comes with the sentence. Saying a sheet may be wrong is free; giving somebody the means to show it has to be built again for every form it is used on.
breaks: It produces nothing on its own and is only ever an addition. The sentence fits anywhere, 800x480 included. Where it fails is on forms whose test is not exhaustive: with squares cut out by scissors, a piece in the wrong place still rests there, so «it does not close» is evidence and not proof, and the sheet should say which of the two it is offering.
